message.content: {"14597_8353800528984": {"answer": "C", "reason": "The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral, symmetric hilar lymph node enlargement with well-defined margins and clear lung fields, which is the classic radiographic presentation of Stage I sarcoidosis."}, "14597_8353800529053": {"answer": "C", "reason": "Stage I sarcoidosis is characterized by bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy (BHL), which is frequently accompanied by right paratracheal lymph node enlargement (the Garland triad or 1-2-3 sign)."}, "14597_8353800544728": {"answer": "A", "reason": "The most prominent finding is bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy without parenchymal infiltrates, which defines Stage I sarcoidosis according to the Scadding staging system."}}
